hypotheses.justification: Not used in the statement. Without it the claim still holds: any DVR A whose fraction field L is a number field has finite residue field. (1) Some prime q lies in the maximal ideal m: otherwise every nonzero integer is a unit in A, so ℚ ⊆ A; A is integrally closed and L is algebraic over ℚ, so A = L, a field, which is impossible for a DVR. (2) A contains O_L, since its elements are integral over ℤ ⊆ A and lie in L = Frac A. (3) P = m ∩ O_L is a nonzero prime (it contains q), hence maximal in the Dedekind ring O_L. (4) A is local and dominates the valuation ring (O_L)_P with the same fraction field; if some x ∈ A were not in (O_L)_P, then x⁻¹ would lie in the maximal ideal of (O_L)_P, hence in m, so x would be both a unit and a non-unit of A. Thus A = (O_L)_P. (5) The residue field is O_L/P, which is finite. L is a number field here because it is ℚ(ζ_p). The current proof uses hAp only for the CharP / ℤ-surjectivity shortcut; the argument above replaces it. This proof is a sketch and has not been formalised.

Not needed for the statement to elaborate (IsCyclotomicExtension {p} ℚ L needs no primality). For any p, L is a number field: for p = 0 the definition only uses nonzero n ∈ S, so the roots generate nothing and L = ℚ; for p = 1, hAp says 1 lies in the maximal ideal, impossible, so the statement is vacuous; for p ≥ 2, L = ℚ(ζ_p) is finite over ℚ. The general argument given for hAp (a DVR with number-field fraction field equals (O_L)_P for a maximal ideal P of O_L, so its residue field O_L/P is finite) then proves the conclusion without primality. The current proof uses primality only through ZMod p / CharP and the cyclotomic surjectivity lemma, which this argument replaces. The argument also seems to allow deleting this hypothesis together with hAp. This proof is a sketch and has not been formalised.
